     9	/-!
    10	# Finite subsets in affine opens
    11	
    12	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` is the action-free geometric condition behind the
    13	finite-Galois quotient construction: every finite subset of `X` lies in one
    14	affine open.  For a finite Galois extension, this immediately supplies
    15	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` for every action on `X`.
    16	
    17	The property is stated independently of Picard data.  In particular, it is a
    18	conclusion to be proved for a representing scheme, not an additional field of
    19	the representability datum.
    20	-/

    22	set_option autoImplicit false

    24	universe u

    27	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

    31	/-- Every finite subset of a scheme is contained in a single affine open. -/
    32	def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
    33	  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1
    34	
    35	/-- An affine scheme satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    36	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    37	    FiniteInAffine X :=
    38	  fun _ _ ↦ ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ _ ↦ trivial⟩
    39	
    40	/-- `FiniteInAffine` is invariant under isomorphism. -/
    41	theorem finiteInAffine_of_iso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ≅ Y)
    42	    (h : FiniteInAffine X) : FiniteInAffine Y := by
    43	  intro s hs
    44	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (e.hom.base ⁻¹' s)
    45	    (hs.preimage (TopCat.homeoOfIso ((Scheme.forgetToTop).mapIso e)).injective.injOn)
    46	  refine ⟨⟨e.hom ''ᵁ U.1, U.2.image_of_isOpenImmersion e.hom⟩, ?_⟩
    47	  intro y hy
    48	  exact ⟨e.inv.base y, hU (by simpa using hy), by simp⟩
    49	
    50	/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along an affine morphism. -/
    51	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    52	    [IsAffineHom f] (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    53	  intro s hs
    54	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)
    55	  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx ↦ hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩
    56	
    57	/-- An object affine over a field spectrum satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    58	theorem finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom {k : Type u} [Field k]
    59	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsAffineHom X.hom] :
    60	    FiniteInAffine X.left :=
    61	  haveI := isAffine_of_isAffineHom X.hom
    62	  finiteInAffine_of_isAffine _
    63	
    64	/-- `FiniteInAffine` supplies the orbit condition for every finite-Galois
    65	semilinear action on the scheme. -/
    66	theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
    67	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    68	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    69	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}

    13	/-!
    14	# Smooth morphisms are geometrically reduced
    15	
    16	A smooth morphism of schemes is geometrically reduced: every base change to the spectrum of a
    17	field is reduced. Combined with geometric irreducibility, this upgrades the standing hypotheses
    18	of the Jacobian challenge (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom` and
    19	`GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom`) to `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`, which is what all the
    20	actual geometry of the project consumes.
    21	
    22	The commutative-algebra core is that a standard smooth algebra over a domain is reduced. By the
    23	structure theorem for standard smooth algebras (Stacks 00T7,
    24	`RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.exists_etale_mvPolynomial`), such an algebra `S` is étale over a
    25	polynomial ring `P` over the base. Since `S` is flat over the domain `P`, it embeds into
    26	`Frac(P) ⊗[P] S`, which is formally unramified and essentially of finite type over the field
    27	`Frac(P)`, hence reduced by `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field`.
    28	
    29	## Main results
    30	
    31	* `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain`: a flat, formally unramified algebra,
    32	  essentially of finite type over a domain, is reduced.
    33	* `Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain`, `RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`,
    34	  `Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`: étale/standard smooth algebras over
    35	  domains are reduced.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.isReduced_of_field`: a scheme smooth over `Spec` of a field is
    37	  reduced.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyReduced`: a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced
    39	  (instance), together with the `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyIntegral`: a smooth, geometrically irreducible
    41	  morphism is geometrically integral (instance), together with the
    42	  `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.
    43	
    44	This file is written in mathlib generality and is a candidate for upstreaming.
    45	-/

    47	set_option autoImplicit false
    48	
    49	universe u
    50	
    51	open TensorProduct
    52	
    53	section RingTheory
    54	
    55	/-- A flat, formally unramified algebra, essentially of finite type over a domain, is reduced.
    56	This generalizes `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field` from fields to domains, at the
    57	price of the flatness assumption (which is automatic over a field). -/
    58	theorem Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
    59	    [IsDomain B] [Algebra B S] [Algebra.FormallyUnramified B S] [Algebra.EssFiniteType B S]
    60	    [Module.Flat B S] : IsReduced S := by

    67	        ⇑(TensorProduct.lid B S).symm := by

A bounded, honest conditional bridge is now feasible:


Its explicit quotient specialization should be:


This is the smallest honest next implementation unit: one new Pic0 finite-Galois descent bridge module. It introduces no hypothesis beyond the finite-Galois representation and orbit condition named in the requested theorem.

**What Is Complete**

The quotient geometry is no longer a blocker. The glued quotient has a Type-valued witness at [GaloisQuotientOverlap.lean:1613](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GaloisQuotientOverlap.lean:1613), an `IsGaloisQuotient` theorem at [line 1626](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GaloisQuotientOverlap.lean:1626), and the exact `Over (Spec K)` target at [line 1643](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GaloisQuotientOverlap.lean:1643). **Unconditional Endpoint**

No, the generic quotient engine cannot currently produce unconditional `pic0_representableBy` from already-landed data.

`pic0_sepClosed_representableBy` assumes `[IsSepClosed k]` and returns a representative over that same field at [Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:276](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:276) and [line 378](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:378). It does not provide a finite Galois extension `L/K`, a representative descended to that finite stage, or the orbit condition. The roadmap explicitly records finite-stage spread and the Picard quotient comparison as missing at [Pic0CriticalPath.lean:133](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0CriticalPath.lean:133).

So the bridge module is bounded and worthwhile, but closing `pic0_representableBy` still requires two substantive upstream results: finite-stage spread of the separably closed representative and an orbit-in-affine proof for that finite-stage representative.
